bull.b: The large recurring share of revenue reflects the durability of Intuitive’s installed-base model, where procedures generate repeat instrument and service purchases. This provides revenue visibility, supports customer lifetime economics, and reduces reliance on periodic system placements alone.

Continued expansion of the installed base strengthens Intuitive’s competitive position and creates a broader foundation for future procedures, instruments, accessories, and service revenue. A larger footprint also deepens customer familiarity and supports adoption across specialties and care settings.

Strong free cash flow gives Intuitive substantial capacity to fund research, product development, training, and commercial expansion internally. High cash conversion and a conservative balance sheet also provide resilience while preserving flexibility for shareholder returns and strategic investment.

bear.b: China presents a structural challenge because weaker tenders, rising domestic competition, and pricing pressure can limit system placements and reduce revenue growth in an important market. The fact that da Vinci 5 is not yet cleared there may further constrain product momentum.

Slower growth reduces the pace at which Intuitive can expand its installed base and compound procedure-driven recurring revenue. Although profitability remains strong, a maturing core business makes sustained innovation, new indications, and geographic expansion increasingly important to future growth.

The extended-use instrument program could improve customer economics and support adoption, but it may also weaken the recurring revenue yield from each benign procedure. If broadly adopted, lower replacement frequency could pressure instruments-and-accessories growth and alter the business model’s economics.
